title: U.S. Import and Export Price Indexes, May 2026 (USDL-26-0903)
date_evidence: Transmission of material in this release is embargoed until USDL-26-0903 8:30 a.m. (ET) Tuesday, June 16, 2026
key_claim: US import capital goods prices rose 1.3 percent in May 2026, the largest advance in the monthly series, with computers, peripherals and semiconductors named among the drivers; overall import prices rose 1.9 percent.
frame_summary: The BLS release frames the May move as a broad rise in imported goods prices in which computer and semiconductor categories are a named, load-bearing contributor rather than a curiosity, putting the memory shock inside official price statistics.
verbatim_quote: Import capital goods prices increased 1.3 percent for the month. Higher prices for computers, peripherals, and semiconductors; scientific and medical machinery; and industrial and service machinery drove the advance.
verbatim_list: U.S. import prices increased 1.9 percent in May, the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics reported today, following a 2.0-percent rise in April.

title: Monetary Policy Decision and Opening Remarks to the Press Conference (July 16, 2026)
date_evidence: Monetary Policy Decision & Opening Remarks to the Press Conference (July 16, 2026)
key_claim: The Bank of Korea raised its Base Rate by 25 basis points from 2.50% to 2.75% on 16 July 2026, citing growth strengthened by exports and investment and inflation expected to stay above target for a considerable time.
frame_summary: The Bank treats Korea's export-led boom as a macroeconomic condition requiring tightening, which places the memory cycle inside monetary policy rather than inside a sector narrative.
verbatim_quote: The Monetary Policy Board of the Bank of Korea decided today to raise the Base Rate by 25 basis points from 2.50% to 2.75%.
verbatim_list: Along with economic growth having strengthened, led by exports and investment, inflation is expected to remain above the target level for a considerable time, and financial stability risks also persist.
notes: Fetched live on 2026-08-15. Quote appears in the page description block and decision text.

title: Overdrawn at the memory bank: How AI is creating memory shortage, and what happens next
date_evidence: Overdrawn at the memory bank: How AI is creating memory shortage, and what happens next August 06, 2026
key_claim: J.P. Morgan Global Research estimates DRAM prices will have risen more than 400% from the start of 2024 to the end of 2026, attributes a 0.2 to 0.4 percentage point lift to inflation to the memory shock, and notes hyperscaler long-term agreements running five years or longer reduce fabricators' flexibility to serve consumer goods.
frame_summary: The bank argues that memory has become the binding bottleneck in AI expansion and that the contractual form of hyperscaler demand, not just its size, is what transmits the shock into consumer prices and into security hardware supply.
verbatim_quote: J.P. Morgan Global Research estimates that DRAM prices will have risen more than 400% from the start of 2024 to the end of 2026.
verbatim_list: The Consumer Price Index (CPI) for software and accessories and Producer Price Index (PPI) for storage devices have both risen 23% since the end of 2024.
with the import price index for computers, peripherals and parts up 37%
Every 10% increase in hardware costs is estimated to raise core CPI and PCE inflation by around 0.1%, with a 0.2–0.4% lift to inflation attributed to the shock in memory prices
While LTAs may help keep costs manageable for hyperscalers, they dramatically decrease the flexibility of memory fabricators to address demand for memory chips in consumer goods.

Major cloud providers, or hyperscalers, are consuming most of the available semiconductors, leaving security hardware manufacturers, those making firewalls, intrusion detection systems and secure routers struggling with limited supply and rising costs
notes: Fetched live on 2026-08-15. Page carries meta publishDate 2026-08-06T12:03:05.359-04:00 and a visible dateline of August 06, 2026.

title: Worldwide Smartphone Market to Decline 13.9% in 2026 as Memory Crisis and US-Iran War Constrain Growth
key_claim: IDC forecasts worldwide smartphone shipments falling 13.9% in 2026 to 1.09 billion units, the steepest annual contraction on record, with average selling prices reaching a record $550 and the sub-$100 segment becoming uneconomic.
frame_summary: IDC argues that the memory shock is a permanent cost reset rather than a cyclical squeeze, and that it redistributes share towards vendors that secured supply early while pricing the bottom of the market out of existence.
verbatim_quote: worldwide smartphone shipments are forecast to decline 13.9% year-on-year in 2026 to 1.09 billion units
verbatim_list: elevating smartphone ASP to a record $550, up $100 from last year
Middle East and Africa (MEA) is forecast to drop 23%, Central and Eastern Europe 19%, and Asia Pacific excluding Japan and China (APeJC) 14%

The sub-$100 segment, which accounted for over 170 million devices in 2025, becomes economically unviable as memory and NAND costs settle at a permanently higher level, even after the memory shortage stabilises in 2028.

title: PC Market Enters Volatile Territory as Memory Shortage Persists Through 2027
key_claim: IDC forecasts global PC shipments falling 11.3% in 2026 with a 20% year-over-year drop in the fourth quarter, average selling price growth of 17%, and no relief from the memory shortage before the end of 2027.
frame_summary: IDC argues that PC vendors face a portfolio problem rather than a demand problem: component scarcity, not weak buyers, is what removes configurations and lifts prices, and the constraint runs past 2027.
verbatim_quote: IDC now forecasts global PC shipments will decline 11.3% for the full year, with conditions worsening progressively through Q4, when shipments are expected to fall 20% year-over-year.
verbatim_list: We’re not seeing any relief to the memory shortage situation before the end of 2027, which means prices will continue to rise and PC manufacturers will struggle to maintain full product portfolios for the foreseeable future.
IDC forecasts ASP growth of 17% in 2026, and even as memory capacity expands over the next two years, pricing is unlikely to return to 2025 levels

title: AI Server Demand Continues to Support Memory Prices in 3Q26, but Gains Moderate as Consumer Demand Weakens and High Base Effects Take Hold
key_claim: TrendForce forecasts conventional DRAM contract prices rising 13 to 18% quarter on quarter in 3Q26 and NAND Flash 10 to 15%, with suppliers continuing to reallocate capacity toward server and AI applications and consumer buyers reaching an affordability limit.
frame_summary: TrendForce frames the quarter as a market split in two: AI and server demand still sets supply priority while consumer buyers have stopped absorbing price rises, so the constraint on phones and PCs is allocation rather than willingness to pay.
verbatim_quote: Memory suppliers will continue to deliver the volumes agreed upon with PC OEMs and module makers for 2026, but ongoing capacity reallocations toward server applications are reducing the supply available for PC DRAM.
verbatim_list: Conventional DRAM contract prices are forecast to rise 13–18% QoQ in 3Q26, while NAND Flash contract prices are expected to increase 10–15%
Record-high contract prices mean customers from consumer markets, such as PCs and smartphones, are reaching their affordability limit, leading to more moderate price increases in 3Q26
Nevertheless, suppliers continue to prioritize AI-related applications when allocating production capacity, keeping LPDRAM supply tight and supporting further contract price increases.
notes: Fetched live on 2026-08-15. Also the principal counter-evidence source: consumer price tolerance is the constraint moderating further rises.

title: Automakers Face Memory Shock as AI Uses Up Semiconductor Supply
key_claim: Analysts at Omdia and Gartner describe the 2026 memory shortage as a deliberate reallocation of wafer capacity towards HBM rather than a supply failure, with automotive semiconductors accounting for only about 10% of the market and therefore low in the supply priority order.
frame_summary: EE Times argues that the automotive industry's problem is its rank in the queue rather than the size of the shortage, and that certification timelines and AEC-Q100 qualification make substitution slow enough to force design and inventory changes instead.
verbatim_quote: Automotive semiconductors account for only about 10% of the entire semiconductor market, so from the perspective of the semiconductor industry, they are by no means a high priority.
verbatim_list: the average connected car in 2026 will need about 278 gigabytes of memory to support up to 100 million lines of code
causing DRAM prices to nearly double each quarter and raising the cost to build a premium smart electric car by about $880 to $1,470
Automakers will likely have to slow down the pace of transitioning to advanced autonomous driving systems over the next one to two years

Automotive memory has to pass strict AEC-Q100 tests to ensure it works in extreme temperatures and vibrations, a certification process that can take up to two years and prevents automakers from quickly switching to untested supplies.
notes: Structural anchor: published 93 days before the scan date, just outside the soft 3-month window, and the canonical source for the automotive queue-position framing. Cited inline like any other source.

title: SK hynix Announces 2Q26 Financial Results
key_claim: SK hynix reported record 2Q26 results with a 76% operating margin and confirmed it has finalised long-term supply agreements with around 10 customers, describing timely delivery of requested volumes as a core competitive capability.
frame_summary: The company presents multi-year contracting and capacity discipline as its strategy, which is the supplier-side statement of the same fact the downstream market experiences as rationing.
verbatim_quote: The company has finalized Long-Term Agreements (LTAs) with around 10 customers, including key strategic partners, and is continuing further discussions with major industry clients.
verbatim_list: SK hynix Inc. (or “the company”, www.skhynix.com) announced today that it has recorded 79.3187 trillion won in revenues, 60.5426 trillion won in operating profit (with an operating margin of 76%), and 93.9226 trillion won in net profit, marking an all-time high quarterly performance.
In a market environment where customer demand exceeds supply capabilities, the ability to deliver requested volumes in a timely manner has emerged as a core business competitiveness.
notes: Vendor source, used only as corroboration of the contracting structure and margin position. Fetched live on 2026-08-15.
